issue: Greek 'μαμά μου' is natural, but the gloss 'Good night, my mom.' is a word-for-word calque no English speaker says.

fix.grammar: Καληνύχτα is only for parting at night — greet people in the evening with καλησπέρα.

issue: With σήμερα, 'τι κάνετε σήμερα;' reads as 'what are you doing today?', not the glossed 'how are you today?'. The σήμερα is an English 'how are you today' calque; Greeks just say τι κάνετε;

fix.grammar: Χαίρετε is a polite all-purpose hello, safe with strangers: Χαίρετε, τι κάνετε;

issue: 'Μιλάτε αγγλικά, παρακαλώ;' tacks παρακαλώ onto a yes/no question — an English 'please' calque; no Athenian phrases it this way. The gloss 'Do you speak English, please?' is equally unnatural. The idiomatic opener is συγγνώμη.

fix.english: Excuse me, do you speak English?

issue: Aspect error: 'Αύριο θα μιλάμε πάλι' uses the imperfective future (habitual/ongoing) for a one-time event; a native says θα μιλήσουμε or τα λέμε αύριο. Perfective stems are unavailable to the engine, so the fix uses the very natural colloquial present-as-future.

fix.grammar: Greek uses the present for near plans: Μιλάμε αύριο = We'll talk tomorrow.

issue: Register clash: αντίο sounds final/formal (parting for good), which sits oddly next to the casual 'τα λέμε αύριο'. Everyday Greek pairs τα λέμε with γεια.

fix.grammar: Τα λέμε (literally 'we say them') is the everyday 'see you / talk soon'.

issue: Tip mismatch: the card teaches του = 'his' (and the sentence starts with feminine αυτή), but the tip explains masculine αυτός, which does not appear in the sentence and was already covered on el-0090.

fix.grammar: του = his and follows the noun: η γυναίκα του = his wife.

issue: Tip is factually wrong as stated: 'After the verb, ο becomes τον' — position is irrelevant (subjects follow verbs too: ήρθε ο Νίκος). The article changes because the noun is the object.

fix.grammar: θέλω and έχω take τον for masculine 'the': θέλω τον λογαριασμό = I want the bill.
